title: Cross-modal failover and customer escalation protocol for mixed-hosted/dedicated/private model regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: When model rollouts produce regressions that affect a subset of tenants across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, SRE and the Model Onboarding team need a single coordinated protocol that: (1) identifies the minimal safe failover (model variant / lower-capacity path), (2) prioritizes customer-facing remediation by contract tier and active incidents, and (3) performs state reconciliation (KV cache, prefix caches, request routing) without causing cascading token-rate overloads. This ticket defines the orchestration flow, operational tooling hooks, and customer-communication template for cross-modal failovers.
updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, Onboarding, and Solutions Eng. Collected initial failure modes from last three incidents; emphasis on mixed-deployment propagation differences.

2026-03-03: Prototype 'failover preference map' created to rank fallback paths (model-variant -> quantized-variant -> graceful-degradation API). Stored at https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CROSS-MODEL-FAILOVER.
2026-03-05: Runtime team opened PR #4123 to add a 'graceful-degrade' route header; test harness in GH actions at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4123.
2026-03-08: Performed dry-run with synthetic traffic against a Dedicated pool; observed 12% higher request latency during KV cache reconciliation — instrumenting shard-aware warmup.
2026-03-10: Onboarding confirmed customer-priority list export is available via CRM; added to playbook. Next: finalize rate-limit choreography and oncall handoff checklist.

Links: Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CROSS-MODEL-FAILOVER; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123; Dashboard slice: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/cross-modal-failures
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: SRE assigns incident lead and tags deployment modes affected (hosted/dedicated/private).
2) Snapshot: Immediately capture model variant, commit hash, KV cache head pointers, and active request hashes. Push snapshot to incident bucket.
3) Prioritize: Load customer-priority export and mark customer slices to protect (P0/P1).
4) Apply 'failover-preference-map' to select first safe target: same-architecture variant with conservative quantization -> smaller context length model -> structured-response-only mode.
5) Throttled switch: Execute staged traffic split (5% -> 20% -> 50%) with per-tenant gates, monitor token error rates and latency percentiles.
6) KV reconciliation: Run shard-aware cache rehydration for affected tenants; if mismatches are detected, perform synthetic prefix replays before full traffic migration.
7) Escalate: If degradation persists after 3 staged steps, trigger cross-team bridge and prepare rollback to prior stable model revision.
8) Close: Confirm metrics restored to SLO; run post-change tests; notify customers and close incident playbook with postmortem link.
rollback_steps: Stop staged routing changes and restore traffic to last known-good model config using atomic route flip for Hosted and Dedicated control plane.
For Private deployments, coordinate with customer ops: provide signed config bundle and step-by-step rollback checklist; obtain explicit acknowledgment before flipping.
Reconcile KV caches: mark caches 'stale-to-evict' and initiate background warming against the restored model to avoid cold miss storms.
If rollback involves model weight downgrade, validate tokenization parity and run smoke evals against representative prompt sets before restoring 100% traffic.
Notify customers per communication_playbook and schedule a follow-up window for deeper investigation.
kv_cache_reconciliation: Use shard-aware, tenant-scoped cache warming: export keys at snapshot, run parallel warmup runners pinned to the restored model binary, and rate-limit warmup traffic to 1% of production qps to prevent overload. In Private mode, provide a signed warmup bundle and script for customer execution. Implement a checksum diff for KV heads to detect non-deterministic drift.
communication_playbook: Internal: open #inc-rollouts bridge, label affected customers and severity. Post periodic cadence updates: initial triage + 15m + 45m + hourly until stable.

Customer-facing: For impacted customers, send triage update stating: what we observed, immediate mitigation (model fallback/rollback), expected ETA for resolution, and an offer for a dedicated postmortem. Use templated language in Confluence to avoid ambiguity.
Legal/Support: If a P0 affects SLA, alert Customer Success and Legal for contract notifications and remediation options.
test_plan: Unit: kernel selection and model-variant switching tests in CI (coverage for quantized/non-quantized paths).
Integration: staged traffic split simulation in perf lab with multi-tenant synthetic slices mirroring production distributions.
Private validation: create a lightweight VM image and run the rollback script in air-gapped environment to prove signed bundle integrity.
Chaos: schedule a controlled canary failure where the runtime intentionally returns 5xx for a small slice to validate orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook drafted and reviewed by SRE, Runtime, Onboarding, and Support (minimum 4 reviewers).
End-to-end automated test exists that simulates cross-env failover with assertion on SLO restoration within 20 minutes.
Customer-priority export integrated and tested; support can mark and protect at least 10 P0 tenants.
Documentation and customer templates published to Confluence and linked from the Console incident modal.
postmortem_actions: Add metric-level alerts for pre-fail signals discovered during runs (e.g., rising entropy in model logits, sudden KV head divergence).
Add the 'failover-preference-map' to the model catalog UI so product can override defaults for specific customers.
Schedule a 2-hour runbook drill with Oncall and Solutions Eng every quarter; record and iterate on gaps discovered.
Follow up ticket: ENG-863211 (implement checksum diff tooling for KV head validation).
